meta.title: What is Unlawful Content: Cybercrime Report & Tracking
meta.description: A factual explanation of what counts as unlawful online content in India, and what to do if you see it.

title: What is Unlawful Content
subtitle: A plain-language explanation of what this term covers, and what to actually do if you come across it.
heroImageAlt: A hand holding a smartphone in a bright, plant-filled office.

categoriesItems.title: Child sexual abuse material (CSAM)
categoriesItems.body: Any image, video, or material that sexually exploits a child. This is illegal to create, possess, view, or share, without exception, anywhere in India.

categoriesItems.title: Non-consensual intimate imagery
categoriesItems.body: Private or intimate images or videos of a real person shared, or threatened to be shared, without their consent, including deepfakes made to look like a real person.

categoriesItems.title: Content that incites violence or hatred
categoriesItems.body: Material that promotes communal violence, terrorism, or hatred against a group, or that calls for real-world harm against specific people.

categoriesItems.title: Content that violates the IT Act, 2000
categoriesItems.body: India's Information Technology Act sets out further categories of unlawful electronic content, including certain kinds of impersonation and content threatening public order.

safetyNoteTitle: Important: how to report it safely
safetyNoteBody: If you come across content like this, especially CSAM, do not download, save, or forward it, even to report it. Sharing it further can itself be a criminal act, regardless of intent. Use the platform's own report button, or report the URL/account directly to the authorities, without keeping a copy yourself.
whatToDoTitle: What to do if you see it

whatToDoItems.title: Report it on the platform first
whatToDoItems.body: Every major platform has an in-app or on-page report option for exactly this. That report reaches the platform's own trust and safety team directly.

whatToDoItems.title: Report it to the real national portal
whatToDoItems.body: cybercrime.gov.in has a dedicated reporting path for unlawful content, separate from the financial fraud journey.

whatToDoItems.title: Call 1930 if you or someone else is at immediate risk
whatToDoItems.body: If the content involves an active threat to someone's safety, treat it as urgent.

footer: This page is informational, not a reporting tool. See our <link>Cyber Volunteer Concept</link> page for how citizens support flagging content like this in the real programme.
